p.src: Du Xing then asked, “My benefactor, what business has brought you here?” Yang Xiong leaned close and whispered, “I killed a man in Jizhou and intended to go join the band at Liangshan Marsh. Last night we lodged at the Zhu Family Inn. Shi Qian, a companion traveling with us, stole and ate the inn’s cock that announced the dawn. A quarrel with the waiter broke out, and in our fury we set fire to the place and burned it down. The three of us fled through the night, but before we knew it, pursuers were upon us from behind. The two of us speared several of them from their feet, but suddenly two hooked poles shot out of the tangled grass and dragged Shi Qian away. The two of us blundered our way here and were just about to ask directions when, to our surprise, we met you.” Du Xing said, “Do not be alarmed, my benefactor. I shall have Shi Qian released and returned to you.” Yang Xiong said, “Sit with us a while, brother, and share a cup.”

p.src: Du Xing said, “Before Dulong Ridge stand three hills, upon which lie three manors. In the middle is Zhu Family Manor, to the west Hu Family Manor, and to the east Li Family Manor. Together the three villages contain some ten or twenty thousand armed households and men. Zhu Family Manor is the mightiest and stands at their head. Its master is known as Squire Zhu, and he has three sons called the Three Heroes of the Zhu Clan. The eldest is Zhu Long, the second Zhu Hu, and the third Zhu Biao. They also have an instructor called Luan Tingyu, nicknamed ‘Iron Staff,’ a warrior with the courage to withstand ten thousand men. The manor itself commands one or two thousand highly capable retainers. At Hu Family Manor in the west, the master, Elder Hu, has a son called Hu Cheng, nicknamed the ‘Flying Tiger,’ who is also highly formidable; but his daughter is the most heroic of all. Her name is Hu Sanniang, nicknamed ‘Ten-Feet of Steel.’ She wields a pair of Sun-and-Moon sabers and is exceptionally skilled on horseback. The eastern manor here belongs to my master, whose surname is Li and given name Ying. He wields an iron-shafted, steel-tipped spear and carries five throwing knives on his back, with which he can strike a man at a hundred paces, appearing and vanishing like a spirit. The three villages have sworn an oath of life and death. They are united in heart and purpose and come to one another’s aid in fortune or calamity. For fear that the heroes of Liangshan Marsh might come to requisition grain, the three villages have made preparations to resist them. I shall take you both to the manor now. We will see Master Li and ask him to write a letter to rescue Shi Qian.” Yang Xiong asked, “Could your Master Li be Li Ying, known throughout the rivers and lakes as the ‘Sky-Striking Eagle’?” Du Xing replied, “The very man.” Shi Xiu said, “I had only heard it said in the rivers and lakes that a hero named Li Ying, the ‘Sky-Striking Eagle,’ lived on Dulong Ridge. So this is where he is. I have often heard that he is truly formidable and a fine man. Let us go and see him.” Yang Xiong called the tavern keeper over to reckon the bill. But Du Xing would not hear of letting him pay and settled the wine bill himself.

p.src: Around the hour of the Snake, the assistant steward returned. Li Ying summoned him to the rear hall and asked, “Where is the man you went to fetch?” The steward replied, “I saw Squire Zhu in person and delivered the letter. At first he seemed inclined to release the man. But then the Three Heroes of the Zhu Clan came out and flew into a rage. They would neither answer the letter nor release the man, insisting on sending him under guard to the prefectural authorities.” Li Ying exclaimed in astonishment, “Their family and ours, the three villages together, are bound by a pact of life and death. Once my letter arrived, they should have consented. How could matters come to this? You must have explained the matter poorly and brought this about. Steward Du, you must go there yourself, see Squire Zhu in person, and explain the entire affair clearly.” Du Xing said, “I am willing to go. I ask only for a letter written in my master’s own hand; then they will be willing to release him.” Li Ying said, “You are right.” He hurriedly had a sheet of decorated letter paper fetched, wrote the letter himself, and stamped the envelope with his personal name-seal before handing it to Du Xing. A groom led out a swift horse and fitted it with saddle and bridle. Taking up his whip, Du Xing passed through the manor gate, mounted, and galloped toward Zhu Family Manor. Li Ying said, “Set your minds at ease. With this letter in my own hand, they will certainly release him shortly.” Yang Xiong and Shi Xiu thanked him deeply and remained in the rear hall, drinking wine as they waited.

What happened?” Once Du Xing had caught his breath, he said, “I carried my master’s letter to their place and reached the third gate, where I happened upon the three brothers Zhu Long, Zhu Hu, and Zhu Biao sitting together. I bowed three times, but Zhu Biao shouted, ‘What have you come here for again?’ I bent low and reported, ‘My master has sent this letter with his respects.’ That rogue Zhu Biao’s face changed, and he cursed, ‘Your master has no understanding of proper conduct! This morning he sent some insolent wretch here with a letter, demanding the return of Shi Qian, that bandit from Liangshan Marsh. Now that I am about to send him under escort to the prefecture, what do you want here again?’ I said, ‘This Shi Qian is not one of the Liangshan Marsh band. He is a traveler from Jizhou. p.src: Li Ying flew into a rage, spurred his mount, leveled the spear in his hand, and charged straight at Zhu Biao. Zhu Biao urged his horse forward to meet Li Ying in combat. Before Lone Dragon Ridge the two swept back and forth, high and low. After seventeen or eighteen bouts, Zhu Biao could no longer withstand Li Ying; he wheeled his horse and fled. Li Ying galloped after him. Zhu Biao laid his spear crosswise upon his horse, took his bow in his left hand and an arrow in his right, nocked it, drew the bow to the full, and, judging that his pursuer was close enough, twisted backward in the saddle and loosed. Li Ying tried to dodge, but the arrow had already struck his arm. Li Ying somersaulted from the saddle and crashed to the ground. Zhu Biao immediately reined his horse around to seize him. Seeing this, Yang Xiong and Shi Xiu gave a great shout, flourished their two broad-bladed swords, and charged straight at Zhu Biao’s horse. Unable to hold them off, Zhu Biao hastily wheeled his horse to flee, but Yang Xiong thrust his broad-bladed sword into the animal’s hindquarter. p.src: Song Jiang hurriedly remonstrated, “Brother, calm your anger. These two brave men have come a thousand li to join their hearts and strength with ours. How can you have them beheaded?” Chao Gai said, “Since we heroes of Liangshan Marsh overthrew Wang Lun, we have made loyalty and righteousness our guiding principles and shown nothing but benevolence to the common people. Whenever one of our brothers has gone down the mountain, he has never diminished our prestige. Every brother who has joined us, old or new, has borne the splendor of a true hero. But these two scoundrels used the name of Liangshan’s heroes to steal a chicken for food, bringing disgrace upon us all. Today I shall first behead these two and display their heads there as a warning; then we will raise our forces, sweep that village clean, and suffer no loss to our prestige. Men, behead them at once and report back to me!” Song Jiang restrained him, saying, “That will not do. Did you not hear what these two worthy brothers just said? ‘Flea on a Drum’ Shi Qian has always been that sort of man, and it was he who provoked the Zhu family scoundrels. How could these two worthy brothers have intended to sully the stronghold’s name? I too have often heard it said that those scoundrels of the Zhu Family Manor mean to oppose our stronghold. At present our stronghold has many men and horses but lacks money and provisions. It is not we who seek a quarrel with them; rather, those scoundrels have come picking faults with us. This gives us the perfect opportunity to seize them. If we take that manor, we shall gain enough provisions for three or five years. It is not we who are stirring up trouble to harm them; the truth is that those scoundrels have treated us with gross insolence. Brother, set aside your anger for the moment. Though I have little ability, I shall personally lead a force and ask several of our worthy brothers to descend the mountain and attack the Zhu Family Manor. I swear I shall not return to the mountain unless I sweep that village clean. First, we shall avenge the stronghold and preserve our prestige; second, we shall save this lesser brother from being humiliated by them; third, we shall obtain a great store of provisions for the stronghold; and fourth, we can invite Li Ying to come up the mountain and join our band.” Scholar Wu said, “Brother Gongming’s proposal is excellent. How can the stronghold be allowed to cut down men who are its own hands and feet?” Dai Zong added, “Better to behead me than to bar the path of worthy men.” All the chieftains earnestly pleaded with him, and only then did Chao Gai spare the two men. Yang Xiong and Shi Xiu also apologized for their offense. Song Jiang soothed them, saying, “Worthy brothers, do not take this amiss. These are the stronghold’s commands, and matters must be handled in this way. Even if Song Jiang himself committed an offense, he too would have to be beheaded; no favoritism would be permitted. We have recently appointed ‘Iron-Faced Registrar’ Pei Xuan to head the Office of Military Discipline. Fixed rules are already in place for rewarding merit and punishing offenses. You must forgive us—please forgive us.” After Yang Xiong and Shi Xiu had bowed and finished apologizing, Chao Gai ordered them to take seats below Yang Lin. When all the underlings in the stronghold had been summoned to pay their respects and congratulate the new chieftains, cattle and horses were slaughtered and a celebratory banquet was prepared. Two sets of quarters were assigned to Yang Xiong and Shi Xiu for their rest, and ten underlings were allotted to attend each man. That evening the banquet came to an end. The next day another banquet was prepared, and the company gathered to discuss their plans.

p.src: Song Jiang ordered the Iron-Faced Registrar, Pei Xuan, to calculate how many men should descend the mountain. He then summoned the chiefs to discuss accompanying him in an attack on the Zhu Family Manor, determined to sweep that village clean. Once the plan was settled, Chao Gai alone was to remain in command of the stronghold, while Scholar Wu, Liu Tang, the three Ruan brothers, Lü Fang, and Guo Sheng were left behind to defend the main camp. All those already assigned to guard the shores, passes, and inns were to remain at their posts. The newly arrived chief Meng Kang was assigned to oversee shipbuilding, taking Ma Lin's place as supervisor of the warships. A proclamation was written dividing the chiefs descending the mountain to attack the Zhu Family Manor into two columns. The first consisted of Song Jiang, Hua Rong, Li Jun, Mu Hong, Li Kui, Yang Xiong, Shi Xiu, Huang Xin, Ou Peng, and Yang Lin. Leading three thousand foot soldiers and three hundred cavalry, they donned their armor, descended the mountain, and advanced. The second column consisted of Lin Chong, Qin Ming, Dai Zong, Zhang Heng, Zhang Shun, Ma Lin, Deng Fei, Wang the Short Tiger, and Bai Sheng. They too led three thousand foot soldiers and three hundred cavalry, following behind as support. At the two lesser strongholds of Golden Sands Strand and Duck's Beak Strand, only Song Wan and Zheng Tianshou were ordered to keep guard and arrange the supply of provisions. After seeing them off, Chao Gai returned to the stronghold.

With a little over a li still to go, the vanguard established a stockaded camp. Seated in the central command tent, Song Jiang conferred with Hua Rong: “I hear that the paths inside the Zhu Family Manor are extremely tangled. We must not advance yet. First send two men to investigate every turn of the roads and learn which ways are passable and which are not; only then shall we go in and engage them.” Li Kui said at once, “Brother, I have been idle for a long time and have not killed a single man. Let me go there first.” Song Jiang replied, “Brother, you cannot go. When it is time to break their formation and charge the enemy, I shall send you first. But this is a spy's task, and you are of no use for it.” Li Kui laughed. “For a wretched manor like that, why need you trouble yourself, brother? Just let me take two or three hundred lads and charge in. We will cut down everyone in the cursed place. Why send anyone to scout first?” Song Jiang shouted, “Stop talking nonsense, you fool! Go stand aside. I shall call you when you are needed.” Li Kui walked away, muttering to himself, “Why make such a fuss over swatting a few flies?” Song Jiang then summoned Shi Xiu and said, “Brother, you have been there before. Go there once with Yang Lin.” Shi Xiu replied, “Now that you have brought so many troops here, brother, how could the people of the manor not be on their guard? Before he had traveled twenty li, he found the paths so tortuous and tangled, winding alike in every direction amid dense groves, that it was impossible to tell the way. Shi Xiu therefore set down his load and stopped. He heard the ritual ring sounding ever closer behind him. Looking back, Shi Xiu saw Yang Lin approaching along the road, wearing a battered bamboo hat and an old Daoist robe, and shaking the ritual ring in his hand. Seeing no one else nearby, Shi Xiu called Yang Lin to a halt and said, “The paths here are so winding and confused that I cannot tell which one I took the other day when I followed Li Ying. It was already late then, and all his men knew the roads, so I did not look closely.” Yang Lin said, “Never mind whether the paths are straight or crooked. Just choose the broad roads and follow them.” Shi Xiu shouldered his firewood again and continued along the broad road. Ahead he saw a village with several taverns and butcher shops. Shi Xiu carried his firewood to the front of a tavern and set it down. He saw swords and spears planted outside every shop. Each man wore a yellow vest bearing the great character “Zhu,” and all the passersby were dressed the same. Seeing an elderly man, Shi Xiu bowed respectfully and said, “Good sir, may I ask what custom you follow here? Why does everyone plant swords and spears before the door?” The old man said, “Where have you come from, traveler? Since you know nothing of the matter, you had best leave quickly.” Shi Xiu said, “I am a date merchant from Shandong. I lost my capital and could not return home, so I came here to sell firewood. I know nothing of the customs or geography of this place.” The old man said, “Go quickly and hide somewhere else. A great battle will break out here before long.” Shi Xiu asked, “How could such a fine village as this become the scene of a great battle?” The old man said, “Traveler, can it be that you truly have not heard? I shall tell you. This place is called Zhu Family Village, and the residence of Squire Zhu stands upon the ridge. The manor has now incurred the enmity of the heroes of Liangshan Marsh, who have brought their troops to the village entrance and mean to attack us. But they fear the tangled roads inside our village and have not dared enter; at present they are encamped outside. The Zhu Family Manor has issued orders that every household ready its able-bodied young men, so that whenever the command comes, we may go to give support.” Shi Xiu asked, “Good sir, how many households are there altogether in your village?” The old man replied, “Our Zhu Family Village alone has some ten or twenty thousand households, and there are two other villages to our east and west that will support us. The eastern village belongs to Li Ying, the great lord known as the Sky-Swooping Eagle. The western village is Old Master Hu's manor. He has a daughter named Hu Sanniang, nicknamed Ten Feet of Steel, who is exceedingly formidable.” Shi Xiu said, “If that is so, why should you fear Liangshan Marsh?” The old man replied, “Even our own people, when they first arrive and do not know the roads, are liable to be caught.” Shi Xiu asked, “Good sir, why would newcomers be caught?” The old man said, “There is a verse about the roads in our village: ‘Fine indeed is the Zhu Family Manor, where every road twists round and round. It is easy enough to enter, but there is no way out.’” On hearing this, Shi Xiu began to weep. Throwing himself to the ground, he bowed to the old man and said, “I am a traveler who lost his capital and cannot return home. If I sell my firewood and then run into the fighting, unable to escape, would that not be a bitter fate? Grandfather, please take pity on me. I will gladly give you this load of firewood if you will only show me the way out.” The old man said, “How could I take your firewood for nothing? I shall buy it from you.

Seeing no one else nearby, Shi Xiu called Yang Lin to a halt and said, “The paths here are so winding and confused that I cannot tell which one I took the other day when I followed Li Ying.
It was already late then, and all his men knew the roads, so I did not look closely.”
Yang Lin said, “Never mind whether the paths are straight or crooked. Just choose the broad roads and follow them.”
Shi Xiu shouldered his firewood again and continued along the broad road. Ahead he saw a village with several taverns and butcher shops.

Shi Xiu carried his firewood to the front of a tavern and set it down. He saw swords and spears planted outside every shop. Each man wore a yellow vest bearing the great character “Zhu,” and all the passersby were dressed the same.
Seeing an elderly man, Shi Xiu bowed respectfully and said, “Good sir, may I ask what custom you follow here?
Why does everyone plant swords and spears before the door?”
The old man said, “Where have you come from, traveler?
Since you know nothing of the matter, you had best leave quickly.”
Shi Xiu said, “I am a date merchant from Shandong. I lost my capital and could not return home, so I came here to sell firewood. I know nothing of the customs or geography of this place.”
The old man said, “Go quickly and hide somewhere else. A great battle will break out here before long.”
Shi Xiu asked, “How could such a fine village as this become the scene of a great battle?”
The old man said, “Traveler, can it be that you truly have not heard? I shall tell you.
This place is called Zhu Family Village, and the residence of Squire Zhu stands upon the ridge.
The manor has now incurred the enmity of the heroes of Liangshan Marsh, who have brought their troops to the village entrance and mean to attack us.
But they fear the tangled roads inside our village and have not dared enter; at present they are encamped outside.
The Zhu Family Manor has issued orders that every household ready its able-bodied young men, so that whenever the command comes, we may go to give support.”
Shi Xiu asked, “Good sir, how many households are there altogether in your village?”
The old man replied, “Our Zhu Family Village alone has some ten or twenty thousand households, and there are two other villages to our east and west that will support us.

The eastern village belongs to Li Ying, the great lord known as the Sky-Swooping Eagle. The western village is Old Master Hu's manor. He has a daughter named Hu Sanniang, nicknamed Ten Feet of Steel, who is exceedingly formidable.”
Shi Xiu said, “If that is so, why should you fear Liangshan Marsh?”
The old man replied, “Even our own people, when they first arrive and do not know the roads, are liable to be caught.”
Shi Xiu asked, “Good sir, why would newcomers be caught?”
The old man said, “There is a verse about the roads in our village: ‘Fine indeed is the Zhu Family Manor, where every road twists round and round.
It is easy enough to enter, but there is no way out.’”

On hearing this, Shi Xiu began to weep. Throwing himself to the ground, he bowed to the old man and said, “I am a traveler who lost his capital and cannot return home. If I sell my firewood and then run into the fighting, unable to escape, would that not be a bitter fate?
Grandfather, please take pity on me. I will gladly give you this load of firewood if you will only show me the way out.”
The old man said, “How could I take your firewood for nothing?
I shall buy it from you.

p.src: Come inside for now, and let me offer you some wine and food.”

p.src: Shi Xiu thanked him, shouldered the firewood, and followed the old man into the house. The old man warmed two bowls of clear wine and served a bowl of millet gruel for Shi Xiu to eat. Shi Xiu bowed again in thanks and said, “Grandfather, please tell me the way out.” The old man said, “Go on through the village. Whenever you see a white poplar, turn there, regardless of whether the road is broad or narrow. Every turning marked by a white poplar is a way through; where there is no such tree, the road is a dead end. A turning marked by any other tree is no way through either. If you take a wrong turn, you will wander left and right and never find your way out. Moreover, bamboo spikes and iron caltrops lie buried along the dead-end paths. If you go astray and tread on a springing spike, you are certain to be caught; where then could you flee?” Shi Xiu bowed his thanks and asked, “Grandfather, what is your honorable surname?” The old man replied, “Most people in this village are surnamed Zhu, but my compound surname is Zhongli, and my family has long lived here.” Shi Xiu said, “I have had my fill of your wine and food. One day I shall repay you generously.”

p.src: As they were speaking, a commotion arose outside. Shi Xiu heard people saying that a spy had been captured. Shi Xiu was startled. When he followed the old man outside to look, he saw seventy or eighty soldiers approaching with a man’s arms bound behind his back. When Shi Xiu looked closely, he saw it was Yang Lin, stripped stark naked and bound with rope. At the sight, Shi Xiu secretly groaned in dismay, then casually asked the old man in a low voice, “What sort of man have they captured? Why have they bound him?” The old man replied, “Did you not hear them say he was a spy sent by Song Jiang?” Shi Xiu asked again, “How did they manage to capture him?” The old man said, “That fellow was remarkably bold. He came alone to spy on us, disguised as an exorcist, and slipped into the village. But he did not know the roads and chose only the broad ones. Wandering left and right, he kept taking dead ends, for he knew nothing of the secret of turning at the white poplars. People saw that he kept taking wrong turns and found his arrival suspicious, so they reported him to the masters of the manor, who came to seize him. Only then did the fellow draw a sword and, with a sweep of his hand, wound four or five men. But he could not withstand so many people. They all rushed him at once, and so he was captured. Someone recognized him as an old outlaw called Yang Lin, the ‘Brocade Leopard.’”

p.src: Before he had finished speaking, cries clearing the way sounded ahead, and word came that the manor’s Third Young Master was approaching on patrol. Peering through a crack in the wall, Shi Xiu saw twenty pairs of tasseled spears arrayed in front, while behind them rode four or five men on warhorses, all carrying strung bows and arrows. There were also three or five pairs of scouts on dappled horses. In their midst rode a young warrior upon a snow-white steed, fully equipped with bow and arrows and holding a silver spear. Shi Xiu recognized him, but deliberately asked the old man, “Who is that young lord who just passed?” The old man replied, “That is Zhu Chaofeng’s third son, Zhu Biao. He is betrothed to ‘Ten Feet of Blue’ of the Hu Family Manor in the western village. Of the three brothers, he is by far the most formidable.” Shi Xiu bowed in thanks and said, “Good grandfather, please guide me to the road out.” The old man said, “It is late today. If fighting breaks out ahead, you may throw your life away for nothing.” Shi Xiu said, “Grandfather, please save my life.” The old man replied, “Rest at my house tonight. Tomorrow, once we learn that all is quiet, you may leave.” Shi Xiu bowed his thanks and remained in the house. Presently four or five relays of mounted messengers came past the door, giving orders from house to house: “You villagers, tonight watch for the red lantern as your signal. Unite your strength to capture the outlaws of Liangshan Marsh, then deliver them to the authorities and claim your rewards.” After the messengers had passed, Shi Xiu asked, “Who was that man?” The old man replied, “That official is the local patrol inspector charged with suppressing bandits. He has arranged to capture Song Jiang tonight.” Hearing this, Shi Xiu pondered awhile. He asked for a torch, bade the old man good night, and went to sleep by himself in a nest of straw behind the house.

p.src: Meanwhile, Song Jiang’s troops were encamped at the village entrance. When neither Yang Lin nor Shi Xiu returned to report, he sent Ou Peng after them as far as the entrance. Ou Peng came back and reported, “I heard a commotion in there and people saying that a spy had been caught. The paths looked tangled and difficult to distinguish, so I dared not venture deep into that dangerous ground.” When Song Jiang heard this, he said angrily, “How can we wait for their report before advancing? Now that another spy has been captured, both our brothers must have fallen into their hands. Tonight we must press our attack and fight our way inside, if only to rescue those two brothers. What do you commanders think?” Li Kui immediately said, “I will fight my way in first and see what happens!” On hearing this, Song Jiang at once issued his military orders and told all the soldiers to arm themselves. Li Kui and Yang Xiong formed the vanguard; Li Jun and the others led the rear guard; Mu Hong held the left and Huang Xin the right; while Song Jiang, Hua Rong, Ou Peng, and the other commanders occupied the center. Waving banners and raising battle cries, beating drums and sounding gongs, they charged toward the Zhu Family Manor with great swords and broad axes. By the time they fought their way onto Dulong Ridge, dusk had fallen. Song Jiang urged the vanguard forward to assault the manor. Li Kui of the vanguard stripped himself stark naked, brandished his pair of steel-edged battle-axes, and rushed furiously forward. When he reached the front of the manor, he saw that the drawbridge had already been hauled high and that not a glimmer of light showed inside the gates. Li Kui was about to enter the water and cross when Yang Xiong seized him and said, “You must not. They have shut the manor gates, so they must have some scheme prepared. Wait until our elder brother arrives, and we will discuss another plan.” But Li Kui could not contain himself. Clashing his two axes, he stood across the water and cursed loudly, “You damned old thief, Squire Zhu! Come out! Your grandfather the ‘Black Whirlwind’ is here!” There was no response from the manor. When Song Jiang arrived with the central army, Yang Xiong went to meet him and reported that neither troops nor men could be seen in the manor and that there was no movement at all. Song Jiang reined in his horse and looked. Seeing neither weapons nor troops in the manor, he grew suspicious and suddenly realized, “I have made a mistake. The Heavenly Book plainly warned me not to be rash or impetuous when facing an enemy. I lost sight of that for a moment. Thinking only of rescuing our two brothers, I advanced through the night and never expected to penetrate so deeply into dangerous ground. Now we have come right before their manor without seeing an enemy soldier. They must have some scheme prepared. Order the whole army to withdraw at once.” Li Kui shouted, “Brother, our army has come this far, so do not retreat! I will fight my way across first; all of you follow me!”

p.src: Before he had finished speaking, the people in the manor had already learned of their presence. Suddenly, a signal cannon sounded within Zhu Family Manor, its shot soaring halfway to the heavens. At once, a thousand torches were lit upon Dulong Ridge, while crossbow bolts rained down from the gate tower. Song Jiang hastily ordered his troops to withdraw by the way they had come. Just then, Li Jun, commanding the rearguard, raised an alarm with his men and reported, “The road by which we came has been completely blocked. There must be an ambush.” Song Jiang ordered his troops to search in every direction for a way out. Li Kui brandished his twin axes and rushed to and fro seeking someone to fight, but not a single enemy soldier was to be seen. Then another cannon fired from the summit of Dulong Ridge. Before its reverberations had died away, battle cries erupted on every side and shook the earth, leaving Song Gongming staring open-mouthed, utterly at a loss. Though you possess all the arts of civil and military strategy, how can you escape this net spread over earth and heaven? A scheme to bind tigers and capture dragons has been laid, all to seize the man who makes heaven start and earth tremble. How Song Gongming and the other chieftains ultimately escaped will be revealed in the next chapter.
